Show HN: Disposable – Share small AI-made tools so others can rebuild them
items.summary: I made a site for sharing small tools made with AI. With agents, it is now quick to build a tool that fits your own task. But those tools usually get thrown away after use, and the next person who may needs something similar start again from zero. So I thought maybe if result or process could shared by text or code and this can lead to kind of token sharing economy. Its name is Disposable and compared to "Open source", I named its philosophy to "Open Disposable". So the principle is "Like open source, without the upkeep. Keep the know-how, rebuild the tool your way". You can share anything you actually used and found useful, with no promise to maintain it. Others can use it as is, or give the spec that comes with it to theur own agent and have it rebuilt. If you have your own skill, prompt, or program you would like to show others, please share it. If you get stuck while sharing, let me know. Repo: https://github.com/x-ify/disposable

items.title: Show HN: Robotics needs better CAD, so I wrote a B-rep kernel and 3,487 tests
items.summary: Hey HN, I’m Tony. I’m a co-founder of Springcraft, where we have been doing a lot of CAD modeling for robot parts. Our team kept running into limitations with existing kernels, and so I decided to write a new B-rep kernel and a new comprehensive, kernel-agnostic B-rep conformance test suite. Both are available today under MIT licenses. The kernel, springrep, is written in safe Rust with no dependencies. It covers a broad range of our mechanical CAD needs, including advanced fillets, sweeps, lofts, shells, offsets, STEP and exact measurements and queries. Claude Code made it feasible to write this, but it took a lot of time and care to get it right. The test suite, brep-conformance, has 3,487 cases covering the modeling operations common across kernels: booleans, fillets, chamfers, shells, offsets, sweeps, lofts, STEP, and queries with expected answers coming from closed forms and exact geometry. It caught hundreds of bugs, edge cases, and hot spots in springrep that our own tests had missed, and now springrep passes all of it. We’ve also run it on a few popular open-source kernels and anyone can run it on theirs. This is the first version, so there are surely mistakes in the test and adapters. Corrections, pull requests, and new kernels are welcome. kernel: https://github.com/springcraft-ai/springrep conformance suite: https://springcraft-ai.github.io/brep-conformance/
